groups.subject: Merge blocked as fgos-write-rejected when a stale worker branch never touched .fgos/ but main changed it after the fork (the catchup/approve deadlock and the branchHeadAtTake trust fix).
events.jsonl history silently lost when a git stash/checkout/reset on the shared main checkout reverts the tracked log under live appends: detection, truncation guard, and recovery.
events.jsonl corrupted by hand-resolving git merge conflicts on the tracked log, breaking seq contiguity, and how to resolve such a conflict.
What to do when take/pick/approve refuses with lock-held on main-checkout.lock: check holder liveness and TTL, clear a stale lock with unlock, or wait out a live holder.
main-checkout.lock reporting AMBIGUOUS (unparseable content) on claim: the non-atomic write window that caused it and the inline retry that self-heals it.

The pre-commit hook acquires main-checkout.lock and never releases it, so the lock stays held after commits and blocks other sessions (release-on-exit opt-in, shorter hook TTL, early release in sweep loops).
A worktree-isolated session's Bash guard refuses the compound out-of-process dispatch command, and the fix is a generated wrapper script.
reclaimOrphanedCheckout must not force-remove a worktree that is still live (uncommitted work or a session standing inside it).
A claim worktree goes stale when its branch is moved underneath it (e.g. a child merged into the root branch) and must be resynced on re-entry instead of trusted.
The worktree-isolation race when fanout dispatches agents concurrently into existing worktree paths, and why it is handled as a recoverable self-heal.
State-writing fgos verbs (merge, approve, sync-root, ask, move...) run from inside a linked worktree find no .fgos/ store and must refuse or be pointed at the main checkout.
Approve merge conflicts caused by two in-flight branches claiming the same next decision ID, resolved by hand or by the auto-resolver.
The verify-fail-post-merge block on approve and its recovery playbook (diagnose unrelated failure, self-diagnose in merge-loop, retry through awaiting-approval).
Where merge self-recovery playbooks live: scattered per skill, then a shared reference, then owned by approve itself with merge-loop as a thin caller.
The fgos sync-root verb: why it exists (root-to-main drift window) and its real guards and outcome shape.
Detecting whether an out-of-process worker signaled [DONE]/[BLOCKED] (unsignaled outcome, quoted-token false positive, putting the signal instruction inline in the worker prompt).
Worktree-dispatch attestation: recording what a dispatched worktree actually touched, first advisory-only, then an enforcing halt.
Every Agent/Task or executor dispatch must first ask dispatch decide for the mechanism rather than the skill choosing itself.
Governance over whether an executor may send prompt content to a non-Claude provider (allowCrossProvider and checking real egress, not the command name).
Layout of the herdr-plugin TUI dashboard's work-item and in-process lists (panels, tabs, table columns, sort).
herdr cockpit launch guards keyed on pane labels that were not yet written, so auto-launched panes must be labeled before spawning claude.
The gate-bypass mechanism that lets skill confirmation gates auto-approve: its config shape and why it was designed that way.
False positives in HEAVY_KEYWORDS risk-keyword matching (substring hits, path citations) and the word-boundary fix.
Cleaning up the citation-drift baseline: glossing bare ADR/RUL citations and deleting out-of-home D-ids across the spec docs.
The enduser docs index drifting from the docs on disk, and the doctor check (and its orphan-detection widening) that catches it.
Splitting oversized fgOS skills into SKILL.md plus references under 300 lines and removing bare citations (the design and its per-skill applications).
fgos uninstall: unwiring setup's hooks and shell-rc line, plus the package-removal spike, shipped as two pieces.
Plugin skills locating the fgos CLI in projects that are not a forgent checkout (global/nvm install fallback and self-healing resolution).
return runs an item's verify field as a literal shell command, so placeholder or prose text in it fails as a shell error rather than a test failure.
'Is this item resolved?' checks must use the full resolved-status set (wontfix, delivered, ...) instead of status === 'done'.
Ordering of the clarify/decompose discover pool (pickNextDiscoverItem) used by discover-loop.
Test-suite wall-clock under node --test is set by the slowest file, and what splitting files did and did not buy.
The choke-point survey of decision logic reimplemented in several places, and its ranked priority list.
Failing-test-first evidence for an Iron Law-gated diff: how it is gathered and how to produce it.
Post-land drift among sibling branches after a merge: detecting it from real changed paths and notifying live sessions.
Recording merge provenance (mergedSha/mergedInto) on delivered events, and a merge that landed without it.
Scoring discussion outputs with metrics eval against the discussion-quality rubric.

nearMisses.why: Same fgos-write-rejected error, opposite cause: one is a branch that really committed a .fgos change, the other a stale branch that never touched .fgos.
Both handle an already-merged no-op, but in different verbs and opposite merge directions (catchup pulling the target into the branch vs merging the branch into the target).
Same file name decision-record.md, but one is about restating human-approved decisions to the clarify judge and the other about splitting state.decisions zones.
Both are herdr dashboard layouts, but one is the Rust TUI plugin and the other the browser web dashboard.
Both document a real sort-key order, but for different functions (discover pool pick vs merge/triage impact ranking).
Both start from an 'Unknown skill' error, but one is dev-skills not shipped in the plugin and the other nested project skills invisible to discovery.
Both produced a wrong-branch commit from an out-of-process worker, but one is agy ignoring its spawn cwd and the other dispatch passing the main-checkout cwd.
Share capability/capacity vocabulary, but one unifies tool-registry and dispatch vocabularies into runner.capabilities, the other fixes the capacity for/capability field mismatch.
Both diagnose an unrelated verify failure, but at different steps (return on the branch vs approve's post-merge verify) with different recovery.
Same pool, different procedures: processing one item with discover-next vs sweeping all items with discover-loop and its stop rules.
